What's included

Good floors start with a flat subfloor

Most squeaks, gaps and hollow spots come from what's under the floor, not the floor itself. Before anything goes down we check flatness with a straightedge, screw down loose subfloor and level the low spots.

We install solid hardwood, engineered hardwood, luxury vinyl plank (LVP) and porcelain tile. We aren't tied to one supplier, so the recommendation is based on the room, not on what's in stock.

  • Preparation

    • Removal and disposal of old flooring
    • Subfloor screwed down and levelled
    • Moisture testing on concrete
    • Door jambs undercut

  • Installation

    • Solid and engineered hardwood, nailed, glued or floated
    • LVP floated over underlay
    • Porcelain and ceramic tile over DITRA
    • Stair treads and nosing

  • Finishing

    • New baseboard and quarter round
    • Transitions between rooms
    • Touch-up paint on trim
    • Furniture moved back

  • Materials

    • Supplied by us, or we install yours
    • Samples brought to the site visit
    • Spare boxes left for future repairs
    • Manufacturer warranty paperwork

How we build it

How we install a floor

The install is the quick part. The prep before it decides how the floor feels in five years.

  1. Measure and test

    Square footage measured room by room, and concrete tested for moisture if we're going below grade.

  2. Choose the material

    Samples in your light, in your rooms. We explain the trade-offs so you only pick once.

  3. Acclimatize

    Hardwood and engineered boxes sit in the house for [X] days to adjust to its humidity before installation.

  4. Prep the subfloor

    Old floor out, loose subfloor fixed, low spots levelled.

  5. Install

    Boards or tile down with the right expansion gaps at walls and doorways.

  6. Finish and clean up

    Baseboard, quarter round and transitions installed, site vacuumed, furniture back in place.

Cost

What flooring installation costs

Flooring is priced per square foot of material plus labour. The prep is what surprises people.

  • MaterialLVP, engineered and solid hardwood cover a wide range per square foot.
  • Subfloor workLevelling a sloped floor or replacing water-damaged subfloor adds labour.
  • StairsEach stair is measured and cut on its own, and priced per step.
  • RemovalTearing out glued-down flooring or tile takes longer than carpet.
  • PatternHerringbone and diagonal layouts take more time and more waste.

FAQ

Flooring installation questions

Don't see yours? Call (647) 513-7955. Someone picks up any time, 24/7.

LVP, in most basements. It is waterproof, it floats over the slab and it shrugs off the humidity swings that come with being below grade. Solid hardwood should not go on a concrete slab. Engineered hardwood can work over a dry slab with a proper subfloor if you want real wood underfoot, but it costs more and is less forgiving if water ever gets in.

Yes, if the wear layer is thick enough. A thick wear layer can be sanded and refinished more than once. A thin one may only take a light screen and recoat. We show you the wear layer spec on every product we quote.
